chunks.text: Today we start eigenvalues. An eigenvector of A is a nonzero vector x with A x equal to lambda x, so the matrix only scales it.
The zero vector is excluded. Zero satisfies A x equals lambda x for every lambda, so allowing it would tell us nothing.

Let's do an example. Take A equals the two by two matrix with rows four, one and two, three. A minus lambda I has four minus lambda in the corner and the determinant is lambda squared minus seven lambda plus ten.
So the eigenvalues are five and two. Check the trace: four plus three is seven, five plus two is seven. The product five times two is the determinant ten.
A defective matrix is short of eigenvectors. Take rows one, one and zero, one. Lambda equals one is a double root but there is only one eigenvector, so it cannot be diagonalized.
Why bother diagonalizing? Because A to the k equals X Lambda to the k X inverse. To get A to the hundred you only raise the diagonal entries to the hundred, which is fast.
Announcements. Problem set 3 is due Thursday and the reading for next week is chapter six.
Lecture 18
chunks.heading: Lecture 18

chunks.text: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Definition: A x = lambda x with x not zero. The zero vector is never an eigenvector.
chunks.heading: Definition

chunks.text: Find the eigenvalues: solve det(A - lambda I) = 0. This is the characteristic polynomial.
chunks.heading: The characteristic polynomial

chunks.text: If A has n independent eigenvectors then A = X Lambda X^-1. Then A^2 = X Lambda^2 X^-1 and in general A^k = X Lambda^k X^-1. Powers of A are cheap once you diagonalize.
chunks.heading: Diagonalization and Matrix Powers

chunks.text: The determinant of A is the product of the eigenvalues. Multiply all the lambdas.
chunks.heading: Determinant = Product of lambda's

chunks.text: The trace of A, the sum of the diagonal, equals the sum of the eigenvalues.
chunks.heading: Trace = Sum of lambda's

chunks.text: A matrix needs n independent eigenvectors to be diagonalizable. A defective matrix has too few.
chunks.heading: When can we diagonalize

chunks.text: If A has n independent eigenvectors then A = X Lambda X^-1. Then A^2 = X Lambda^2 X^-1 and in general A^k = X Lambda^k X^-1. Powers of A are cheap once you diagonalize.
chunks.heading: Diagonalization and Matrix Powers

chunks.text: Compute the solution by elimination. Find the pivots, subtract multiples of row one, then find the next pivot of the matrix.
chunks.heading: Elimination

chunks.text: How to compute quickly: use the matrix in upper triangular form and find x by back substitution. Matrix multiplication costs n cubed.
chunks.heading: Back substitution

chunks.text: Find the matrix E that subtracts two times row one from row two. Compute E A to see the effect.
chunks.heading: Elimination matrices

chunks.text: The projection matrix onto the column space of A is P = A (A^T A)^-1 A^T.
chunks.heading: Projection on a subspace

chunks.text: A^T A is invertible exactly when A has linearly independent columns.
chunks.heading: Math: (A^T A) is invertible when A has independent columns

chunks.text: In this section we will look at molarity and dilution. Solutions are everywhere in the lab.
chunks.heading: Molarity

chunks.text: Molarity (M) is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution: M = mol solute / L solution. A 2.0 M NaCl solution holds 2.0 mol in each liter.
chunks.heading: Molarity

chunks.text: Dilution. When a solution is diluted the moles of solute stay the same, so M1 V1 = M2 V2. Diluting 50 mL of 6 M acid to 300 mL gives 1 M.
chunks.heading: Dilution

chunks.text: The empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio of atoms. Convert percent composition to grams, then to moles, divide by the smallest, and multiply to whole numbers.
chunks.heading: Determining empirical formulas

chunks.text: Percent composition by mass is the mass of each element divided by the total mass times 100.
chunks.heading: Percent composition

chunks.text: AMONG the numerous advantages promised by a well constructed Union, none deserves to be more accurately developed than its tendency to break and control the violence of faction.

By a faction I understand a number of citizens, whether amounting to a majority or minority of the whole, who are united by some common impulse of passion, or of interest, adverse to the rights of other citizens.
There are two methods of curing the mischiefs of faction: the one, by removing its causes; the other, by controlling its effects.
A republic, by which I mean a government in which the scheme of representation takes place, opens a different prospect and promises the cure for which we are seeking.
The effect of the first difference is to refine and enlarge the public views, by passing them through the medium of a chosen body of citizens.
Ambition must be made to counteract ambition. The interest of the man must be connected with the constitutional rights of the place.
After an unequivocal experience of the inefficiency of the subsisting federal government, you are called upon to deliberate on a new Constitution for the United States of America.
James Madison argued in Federalist No. 10 that a large republic would control the effects of faction. The paper is one of the most cited.
chunks.heading: Summary

chunks.text:
A random walk takes a step left or right at random. ```julia
function random_walk(n)
    position = 0
    for step in 1:n
        position += rand([-1, 1])
    end
    position
end
```
